description: The high-key boundary, seeded inline. The customer master holds exactly one record and it is the highest key the shipped fixture carries, CUST-ID 000000050 - the fiftieth and last row of app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt, copied into "rows" verbatim rather than sliced out of the fixture by range, so the production-shaped bytes are the seeded bytes (gate G16). app/jcl/CUSTFILE.jcl defines the cluster KEYS(9 0) RECORDSIZE(500 500) INDEXED, and app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl:29-33 selects it ORGANIZATION INDEXED, ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY FD-CUST-ID, so the browse is positioned on the maximum key from its first READ. What the case pins is what happens next: L93 delivers the record with CUSTFILE-STATUS '00', L94 moves 0 into APPL-RESULT and L96 displays the group item, the mainline's own L78 display emits the same record area a second time, and the very next READ reports '10' - so L99 moves 16 into APPL-RESULT, the 88 APPL-EOF condition declared at L63 holds, L108 moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE and the L77 guard suppresses any display for the read that found nothing. Exactly two record lines therefore appear and both are row 50: a translation that wrapped back to the low key, re-read the record it had just delivered, or treated end-of-file as an error would emit a third line, and one that stopped a record early would emit none. The '10' read itself emits nothing at all, which is why the L85 banner follows the pair directly with no end-of-file message between them. The second thing the boundary pins is the width of the key. CUST-ID is PIC 9(09) at bytes 1-9, and the value here is the nine characters 000000050 - not 50, and not 50 followed by seven spaces. Fifty is the one key in this fixture whose significant digits do not fill the span, so an implementation that round-tripped the key through an unpadded integer or right-aligned it as text would produce the wrong bytes on exactly this record and pass on the other forty-nine; the field is named on the final-state channel so that it is reported as a field difference rather than as an unexplained image mismatch. The duplicated display is inherited behaviour and is preserved, not harmonised (practice B5): the L96 display sits inline in the read paragraph's '00' arm with no statement between it and the L78 display in the mainline, so the two lines are adjacent and byte-identical. Sibling CBACT01C reaches its second display through a labelled paragraph and CBACT02C has its own L96 display commented out, so the doubling is a genuine per-program inconsistency rather than a pattern to tidy. The dataset is addressed by the binding key CUSTFILE alone - the name the SELECT assigns it and the name app/jcl/READCUST.jcl STEP05 mounts on its single //CUSTFILE DD - and the DSNAME is resolved from configuration so that no dataset name is written into a case (gate G46). That step is a bare EXEC PGM=CBCUS01C with no PARM anywhere, so "jobParameters" is empty; the program opens CUSTFILE INPUT and issues no WRITE, no REWRITE and no DELETE, so "expectedWrites" is empty as the positive assertion that nothing was written, while the single final-state row read back from the relation asserts that the stored record survived the pass unchanged. RETURN-CODE is never referenced in the program, so L87 GOBACK returns 0 and gate G35 is not exercised here: no abend site is reached and no error literal, rendered file status or ABENDING PROGRAM banner belongs in these lines. R1 caveat: the mandated name CustomerFileReaderJob names a Spring Batch job, but the source Function header reads 'Read and print customer data file' - it computes nothing and writes no dataset. Record layout, taken mechanically from app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy (practice B11): CUST-ID 9(09) at 1-9, CUST-FIRST-NAME X(25) 10-34, CUST-MIDDLE-NAME X(25) 35-59, CUST-LAST-NAME X(25) 60-84, CUST-ADDR-LINE-1 X(50) 85-134, CUST-ADDR-LINE-2 X(50) 135-184, CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 X(50) 185-234, CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD X(02) 235-236, CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD X(03) 237-239, CUST-ADDR-ZIP X(10) 240-249, CUST-PHONE-NUM-1 X(15) 250-264, CUST-PHONE-NUM-2 X(15) 265-279, CUST-SSN 9(09) 280-288, CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID X(20) 289-308, CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD X(10) 309-318, CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID X(10) 319-328, CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND X(01) 329, CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE 9(03) 330-332 and FILLER X(168) 333-500 - summing to exactly 500. On row 50 those spans read CUST-ID 000000050, CUST-FIRST-NAME Aniya, CUST-MIDDLE-NAME Alba, CUST-LAST-NAME Von, CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD OR, CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD USA, CUST-SSN 931248469, CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD 1960-12-01, CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND Y and CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE 623, each stated at its full declared width because a COBOL alphanumeric receiver is space-padded on the right and the padding is part of the record. Per requirement I1 the date-of-birth item is the hyphenated CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD that CVCUS01Y declares; the differently spelled item at the same offset in app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy belongs to the statement copybook modelled separately as Stm03CustomerRecord and is never conflated with this one. The bytes are US-ASCII (practice B8) and custdata.txt matches its copybook width exactly, so this case declares no normalisation. Baseline provenance (practice B12): these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the control flow of app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl, the byte layout app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy declares, the step and DD contract in app/jcl/READCUST.jcl with the cluster attributes in app/jcl/CUSTFILE.jcl, and the real app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt fixture. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, as AAP section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers, and the substituted provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. Gates discharged: G15 (one of the twenty cases this program owns), G16 (the row is the real fixture's own fiftieth line, never synthesised), G18 (the diff count must be zero across all twenty), G19 (the record image is exactly the 500 bytes CVCUS01Y declares), G21 (FILLER is present and space-filled - bytes 333-500 are the 168 spaces named on the final-state channel, so an omitted FILLER shortens the line and fails at once), G47 (the '00' OPEN at L120, one '00' READ, the '10' READ that follows the maximum key and is a normal boundary rather than an error, and the '00' CLOSE at L138) and G51 (the unit is CustomerFileReaderJob driven at tasklet level with CustomerService as the decision-holding collaborator, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path).
